ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZhMxcw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDINe0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 59, "title": "Clock WD2793 Type-II byte transfers independently and correct lost-data handling", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `114f0314231e6191033877f3a035a6c79adb4bf7`, `crates/msx-core/src/disk.rs` advances the sector index when the CPU services DRQ, schedules the next byte 114 cycles afterward, and aborts any unserviced request after 4096 cycles. Read data enters the data register only when read by the CPU. Final-byte service immediately completes the sector.

Consequently, slow polling stretches disk transfers, unread bytes never replace the data register, and later missed writes cannot produce the controller's continued zero-fill behavior. Existing tests enforce some of these approximations. This affects firmware polling and timing-sensitive loaders; no specific commercial-game failure is established.

## Expected outcome

Both Weave and Philips interfaces share device-clocked Type-II transfers. CPU service acknowledges requests without moving media deadlines. Reads continue after overrun; writes distinguish initial starvation from later underrun. Completion and multi-record continuation follow elapsed device time. Preserve existing settling/search behavior and safe private-media ownership.

## Context

Clean local HEAD matches inspected GitHub main. The open Issue/PR collection is empty. [Issue #57](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/57) and [PR #58](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/pull/58) implemented settling/search and explicitly deferred byte cadence and lost-data fidelity.

Inspected technical references:

- [TI second-source TMS279X/WD279X manufacturer transcription](https://deramp.com/swtpc.com/DC_5/TMS279X_DataSheet.pdf), printed pages 7, 11, 20 and 40: register handshakes, 250 kbit/s operation, continued read overrun, initial-write failure and later zero-fill.
- [Pinned openMSX WD2793](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/fdc/WD2793.cc): scheduled transfers, separate initial-write check, extended first-to-second request interval and post-data phases.
- [Pinned upstream raw-sector layout](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/fdc/SectorBasedDisk.cc): synthetic normal MFM headers, gaps and CRC positions. Raw DSK does not supply these timings.

Use these as behavioral evidence with independently authored implementation. Retain existing nine-ID positions; define their phase origin and fixed local header/data offsets explicitly. Adopt the pinned upstream's separate eight-byte initial-write service window as a documented synthetic-profile policy. Physical phase alignment remains unmeasured; earlier WD scan/handbook access failures remain research limitations.

Native disk, Type-I/II and Philips tests plus original CPU/browser fixtures are present. PR #58 and `docs/validation.md` report 236 Rust and 130 browser passes and completed self-review. Current CI step metadata now records successful native and browser checks; detailed logs were not inspected here. Submitted GitHub reviews are empty. Planning ran no builds or tests.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Use cumulative absolute deadlines for nominal 250 kbit/s MFM bytes: 32 microseconds, or 114.54544 CPU cycles at 3,579,545 Hz. Preserve fractional remainder rather than rounding every interval. Publish an explicit timing table for read arrival, initial-write request/check, first-to-second write request, subsequent bytes and completion/CRC tail. Distinguish sourced behavior from selected synthetic offsets.
- [ ] On each read arrival, update the data register and assert DRQ. Replacing an unread byte sets sticky LOST DATA and continues. Reading acknowledges the available byte without shifting future deadlines; repeated reads cannot consume future bytes. Complete by device time even without CPU service. Specify and test final-byte availability, DRQ and IRQ behavior through completion.
- [ ] Abort an initially unserviced write at its distinct initial deadline, with LOST DATA and unchanged media. Once writing starts, consume supplied bytes at scheduled deadlines; later missed requests insert zero, latch LOST DATA and continue. Late service applies to the current request without recovering an already missed position. Do not commit or complete merely because the CPU supplied byte 512.
- [ ] Preserve LOST DATA through normal completion and subsequent multi-record phases until the appropriate new-command/reset transition. Continue multi-record searches from actual completion time, without repeating E settling or automatically crossing tracks. Keep FORCE INTERRUPT status/latching corrections and additional FDC commands outside this task.
- [ ] Retain staged-sector cancellation safety: a completed zero-filled sector commits and becomes dirty if changed; an explicitly canceled incomplete sector is discarded. Update obsolete timeout-safety assertions accordingly. Preserve completed earlier sectors, write protection, exact export, dirty-media guards, reset/media/interface cancellation and prevention of canceled-event resurrection. Document the difference from physical partial-write fidelity.
- [ ] Add independent literal/rational timestamp and payload expectations in the native disk suites. Cover early/late service, one and several missed bytes, initial starvation, resumed writes, final-byte starvation, idle/repeated data accesses, sticky status, multi-record progression and cancellation in every new phase. Compare single-cycle, irregular and large ticks at immediately before/at/after deadlines, including fractional phase and revolution wrap. Tests must not obtain expected timings from production helpers. Record meaningful baseline failures and corrected results.
- [ ] Exercise both bus interfaces on MSX1/MSX2 and both raw geometries. Extend original CPU-executed polling diagnostics to observe overrun/underrun and verify complete payloads and exact exports. Run compiled-Wasm coverage at `/` and `/msx-rust/`; derive polling bounds from the documented timing. Preserve existing video/input, PSG/SCC/SCC-I audio, firmware/sub-ROM/mapper coexistence, SRAM, browser lifecycle and provenance behavior. No BIOS bypasses or proprietary prerequisites.
- [ ] Update affected disk documentation, fixtures and validation records. The Coordinator runs and reports `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test` and `git diff --check`, using README setup. Complete source-Issue/full-diff review and resolve blocking findings before merge. Report passed, failed, skipped and unperformed checks separately.

## Optional validation

Before merge, compare original timestamped register traces with the pinned upstream using the same synthetic layout. Additional software checks may use already lawfully available inputs. These comparisons were not performed during planning; diagnostic success does not establish commercial-game compatibility.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
